Film Room/Heat/What changed

What changed · Miami Heat · through Nov 16

5 straight wins.
Here's what changed.

Miami opened 0-4. Since then the Heat are 8-2, including 5-0 since Erik Spoelstra changed his starting five. At 8-6 they're fourth in the East.

Points per game, from the box scores.

Coach's decision 1

A new starting five.

Ten games in, at Sacramento on Nov 8, Spoelstra changed his starting lineup for the first time: Pelle Larsson in, Andrew Wiggins to the bench. The new five has outscored opponents by 23 points per 100 possessions. Wiggins has given the bench 10.8 points a game over the streak, and rookie Ryan Conwell's minutes have gone up.

Out

Andrew Wiggins

→

In

Still starting

  • Davion Mitchell
  • Klay Thompson
  • Giannis Antetokounmpo
  • Bam Adebayo

Larsson missed the Cleveland and Detroit games with an illness. Miami won both anyway.

Coach's decision 2

Giannis and Bam, split up.

Spoelstra now staggers his two stars' minutes, so each gets long stretches as the main option. With Giannis and Klay Thompson on the floor and Bam resting, Miami has outscored opponents by 31.6 points per 100 possessions.

30.0Giannis points a game, last 5
12.2his rebounds a game
67%his shooting (62 of 92)

Coach's decision 3

More pick-and-roll.

After the 0-4 start, Miami leaned into ball screens: Bam as the main screener and roller, Giannis waiting in the dunker spot instead of crowding the same space. The Heat still use fewer on-ball screens than any team, so it's more structure, not a new offense.

Coach's decision 4

Fewer open threes.

The Heat are switching screens more and mixing in zone. Wide-open threes allowed (no defender within six feet) fell from 16 a game to 9.1, the fewest in the league. Some of the early damage was luck: in the first seven games, opponents' shooting ran about 6 points above what their shot quality predicted, the worst gap in the league.

The breakout

Davion Mitchell runs it.

Mitchell leads all qualified players with 9.2 assists a game, up from 4.1 for his career, and he's at 16.8 points. Over the streak: 17.8 points and 11.0 assists, with a 22-point, 17-assist night against Cleveland. Thompson is shooting 42% on almost 10 threes a game.

11.0Mitchell assists a game, last 5
17assists vs. Cleveland
42%Thompson from three

The catch

The glass, and Bam's hip.

Miami got outrebounded in three of the five wins, and Houston grabbed 21 offensive rebounds on Monday. Bam Adebayo left that game with hip tightness; no timeline yet. Next: Milwaukee on Wednesday, Giannis's first game against his old team, then Oklahoma City on Sunday.

VerdictReal, with a catch: the rebounding.
